label: Inference on Non-Euclidean Spaces
notes: This opening chapter sets the program for the whole book: classical statistics assumes data live in a flat vector space, but directions, axes, and shapes do not. Pages one through seven argue that curved sample spaces demand a genuinely nonparametric and geometric theory of inference rather than a forced linearization.

label: When Data Leave R^n
notes: Three running examples motivate the geometry: unit directions on a sphere, undirected axes in projective space, and configurations of landmarks viewed modulo similarity. Each lives on a manifold, so adding points or averaging coordinates leaves the space. The chapter uses these to show why ordinary moments are ill defined.

label: Directions on the Sphere
notes: Wind directions, geological orientations, and migration headings are unit vectors on the two-sphere. Their arithmetic average has length below one and points into the interior, off the manifold. This simple failure foreshadows the central lesson that meaningful summaries must respect the curved geometry of the sample space.

label: Axes and Shapes
notes: Axial data identify a direction with its negative, living in real projective space, while shape data identify configurations differing by rotation, translation, and scale. Both are quotients of a sphere by a group action, producing the manifolds and metric spaces that occupy the remainder of this book.

label: Shape as a Quotient
notes: Kendall's construction takes k labelled landmarks in the plane, centers and rescales them to a preshape sphere, then quotients by rotation. The resulting shape space is a smooth manifold away from singular configurations, and its non-flat geometry is precisely what makes naive coordinate averaging invalid.

label: The Euclidean Mean Fails
notes: Averaging landmark coordinates or unit vectors componentwise generally yields a point that is not a valid shape or not on the sphere. The chord-based Euclidean mean sits off the manifold, so it cannot serve as a population center. This breakdown is the concrete motivation for the Frechet mean.

label: The Frechet Mean
notes: The Frechet mean replaces the moment definition of average with a variational one: it minimizes the expected squared distance to a random point. On a metric space this object always makes sense, and on Euclidean space it recovers the ordinary mean, so it is a faithful generalization rather than a substitute.

label: Extrinsic vs Intrinsic
notes: Two distances yield two Frechet means. The extrinsic mean embeds the manifold in a Euclidean space, averages there, and projects back, which is fast and stable. The intrinsic mean uses the geodesic Riemannian distance and is coordinate free. The book develops the theory for both throughout.

label: Goals of the Theory
notes: For each notion of mean the book seeks the same statistical triad: consistency of the sample estimator, a central limit theorem describing its fluctuations in a tangent chart, and resulting confidence regions and tests. Establishing these on curved spaces is the technical heart of the nonparametric program.

label: Two-Sample and Bayes
notes: Beyond a single mean, the program extends to comparing two populations through a two-sample test of their Frechet means and to nonparametric Bayesian models that place priors directly on densities over the manifold. These tools answer the applied questions in directional, axial, and shape data analysis.

label: Roadmap of the Book
notes: The book climbs a ladder: metric-space foundations and Frechet means first, then differentiable manifolds with their intrinsic and extrinsic analysis, then Kendall shape spaces as the marquee application, and finally nonparametric Bayes on manifolds. This slide previews how the chapters build on one another.

label: Takeaways
notes: The three lessons to carry forward are that curved data need geometry, that the Frechet mean is the right generalization of the average, and that consistency, central limit theorems, and two-sample or Bayes inference form the recurring agenda. Every later chapter instantiates this pattern on a richer space.
